cards.front: Recall a key point about Democracy in Britain
cards.back: Representative democracy: citizens elect MPs to represent them in Parliament. The UK is a parliamentary democracy where the government is drawn from and accountable to Parliament. General elections must be held at least every 5 years (Fixed-term Parliaments Act 2011, largely repealed 2022).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Democracy in Britain
cards.back: Parliament: House of Commons (650 elected MPs), House of Lords (unelected - hereditary peers, life peers, bishops), and the monarch (largely ceremonial - Royal Assent). Parliament scrutinises the government, passes laws, approves taxation, and represents the public.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Democracy in Britain
cards.back: How a law is made: Green Paper (consultation) -> White Paper (proposals) -> Bill -> First Reading -> Second Reading (debate) -> Committee Stage (detailed examination) -> Report Stage -> Third Reading -> House of Lords -> Royal Assent -> Act of Parliament.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Democracy in Britain
cards.back: Elections: general elections (MPs), devolved elections (MSPs, MSs, MLAs), local elections (councillors), and elections for Police and Crime Commissioners. Voting age: 18 for general elections (16 for Scottish Parliament and Welsh Senedd elections). First Past the Post (FPTP) is used for general elections.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Democracy in Britain
cards.back: Voter turnout and participation: turnout has declined from 84% in 1950 to 67% in 2019. Reasons: disengagement, lack of trust, feeling votes don't matter. Ways to increase participation: lower voting age, proportional representation, online voting, compulsory voting, and citizenship education.

cards.front: Understanding Democracy in Britain in British Context
cards.back: Democracy in Britain is a core topic in GCSE Citizenship Studies that requires understanding of how the UK political and legal systems work, and how citizens can participate effectively. The specification requires you to know how British democracy functions, understand your rights and responsibilities as a citizen, and be able to take informed and responsible action on citizenship issues.

cards.front: Democracy in Britain and UK Democratic Processes
cards.back: The UK is a parliamentary democracy where citizens exercise power through elected representatives. Understanding democracy in britain requires knowledge of how democratic processes work: general elections (first past the post), devolved elections (additional member system for Scotland and Wales), local elections, and referendums. cards.front: Rights, Responsibilities and Democracy in Britain
cards.back: UK citizens have both rights and responsibilities. Key rights include: the right to vote, freedom of speech, freedom of religion, the right to a fair trial, and the right to privacy. These rights are protected by the Human Rights Act 1998, which incorporates the European Convention on Human Rights into UK law.
